hints: Focus on what is really happening first, the halogenoalkane is hydrolysed by water to release a halide ion which then meets silver ions.
Recall your silver halide colours: $\text{AgCl}$ is white, $\text{AgBr}$ is cream and $\text{AgI}$ is yellow, so decide what 2-bromopropane must give.
Compare the $\text{C-Br}$ and $\text{C-I}$ bond strengths to decide which bond breaks more easily and so hydrolyses faster.
walkthrough:
**See the hydrolysis step**

Think of this as a two-stage test. Water first slowly hydrolyses the halogenoalkane to release $\text{X}^-$.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CHXCH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3 + \text{H}^+ + \text{X}^-$$

**Spot the precipitation step**

The released halide then instantly precipitates with silver ions.

$$\text{Ag}^+(\text{aq}) + \text{X}^-(\text{aq}) \rightarrow \text{AgX}(\text{s})$$
So 2-bromopropane releases $\text{Br}^-$ and forms $\text{AgBr}$, which is cream.

**Compare the rate using bond enthalpy**

Hydrolysis involves breaking the carbon-halogen bond. The $\text{C-I}$ bond is longer and weaker than the $\text{C-Br}$ bond, so it needs less energy to break.

Bond strength: $\text{C-F} > \text{C-Cl} > \text{C-Br} > \text{C-I}$
Therefore 2-iodopropane hydrolyses and forms its precipitate faster than 2-bromopropane.

**Put the row together**

Colour from 2-bromopropane is cream, and faster reaction is 2-iodopropane. That combination matches one row exactly.

options.A: Colour is correct, $\text{AgBr}$ is cream, but the rate is wrong. The $\text{C-Br}$ bond is stronger than $\text{C-I}$, so 2-bromopropane is slower, not faster, than 2-iodopropane.
options.B: Both parts are wrong. Yellow is the colour of $\text{AgI}$, not $\text{AgBr}$ from 2-bromopropane, and 2-bromopropane is slower because its $\text{C-Br}$ bond is stronger than $\text{C-I}$.
options.C: Exactly right. 2-bromopropane gives $\text{Br}^-$ which forms cream $\text{AgBr}(\text{s})$, and 2-iodopropane reacts faster because the weaker $\text{C-I}$ bond hydrolyses more readily.
options.D: Rate is correct, 2-iodopropane is faster, but colour is wrong. The question asks for the precipitate from 2-bromopropane, which is cream $\text{AgBr}$, not yellow $\text{AgI}$. This is a common mix-up of the two halides.
